title: 无限梯形网络
statement: 一个向右无限延伸的梯形网络，每一节由串联电阻 1 Ω 和并联电阻 6 Ω 组成（图中 R_1 = R_3 = 1 Ω，R_2 = R_4 = 6 Ω）。
图中只画出前两节，后面无穷多节用一个电阻 R_x 代替——由于去掉前两节后剩下的仍是同样的无限网络，R_x 正好等于整个网络的输入电阻 R_in（数值待求）。
端口 a、b 接电流源 I_s = 9 A。求 R_in、端口电压 u_a、结点 d 的电压 u_d 和 R_4 中的电流 i_4。

questions.explain: 自相似：R_in = 1 + 6 ∥ R_in = 1 + 6R_in/(6 + R_in) → R_in² − R_in − 6 = 0 → R_in = 3 Ω（舍去负根 −2）。
i_4 = u_d / 6 = 2 A；或者：每个结点处电流按 6 Ω 与 3 Ω 分流，并联电阻取 1/3：R_2 中 3 A，R_3 中 6 A，R_4 中 6/3 = 2 A。

hints: 无限网络“少一节还是它自己”：去掉第一节（R_1、R_2）后，并在 R_2 上的那部分网络（从 R_3 开始向右的全部）与从 a、b 看进去的整个网络结构完全一样。
所以 R_in = R_1 + R_2 ∥ R_in，解一个一元二次方程，舍去负根。
知道 R_in 后，每一节都是同一个分压比 / 分流比：在每个结点，并联电阻 6 Ω 与“剩下的网络”R_in 分流。
solution: **1. 自相似方程。** 从 c 向右看（R_2 与其后的无限网络并联），后面那部分正是原网络：R_in = 1 + 6 ∥ R_in = 1 + 6R_in/(6 + R_in)。
**2. 求解。** (R_in − 1)(6 + R_in) = 6R_in → R_in² − R_in − 6 = 0 → (R_in − 3)(R_in + 2) = 0，取 **R_in = 3 Ω**。所以图中 R_x = 3 Ω，有限电路与无限网络完全等效。

en.title: Infinite ladder network
statement: A ladder network extends infinitely to the right; every section consists of a series 1 Ω resistor and a shunt 6 Ω resistor (in the drawing R_1 = R_3 = 1 Ω, R_2 = R_4 = 6 Ω).

Only the first two sections are drawn; the infinitely many remaining sections are replaced by one resistor R_x. Since removing the first two sections leaves the same infinite network, R_x equals exactly the input resistance R_in of the whole network (its value is to be found).
A current source I_s = 9 A drives the port a, b. Find R_in, the port voltage u_a, the voltage u_d of node d and the current i_4 in R_4.

questions.explain: Self-similarity: R_in = 1 + 6 ∥ R_in = 1 + 6R_in/(6 + R_in) → R_in² − R_in − 6 = 0 → R_in = 3 Ω (discard the negative root −2).
Each section multiplies the voltage by 6∥3 / (1 + 6∥3) = 2/3: u_c = 27 × 2/3 = 18 V, u_d = 18 × 2/3 = 12 V.
i_4 = u_d / 6 = 2 A; or: at every node the current divides between 6 Ω and 3 Ω, the shunt taking 1/3: 3 A in R_2, 6 A in R_3, 6/3 = 2 A in R_4.

hints: An infinite network "minus one section is still itself": after removing the first section (R_1, R_2), the part of the network hanging across R_2 (everything from R_3 to the right) has exactly the same structure as the whole network seen from a, b.
So R_in = R_1 + R_2 ∥ R_in; solve the quadratic and discard the negative root.
Once R_in is known every section has the same voltage ratio / current ratio: at each node the 6 Ω shunt shares the current with the "rest of the network", R_in.
solution: **1. Self-similar equation.** Looking right from c (R_2 in parallel with the infinite network behind it), the part behind is the original network again: R_in = 1 + 6 ∥ R_in = 1 + 6R_in/(6 + R_in).

**2. Solve.** (R_in − 1)(6 + R_in) = 6R_in → R_in² − R_in − 6 = 0 → (R_in − 3)(R_in + 2) = 0, so **R_in = 3 Ω**. Hence R_x = 3 Ω in the drawing and the finite circuit is exactly equivalent to the infinite one.
**4. Section by section.** Each section: u_next = u_prev × (6∥3)/(1 + 6∥3) = u_prev × 2/3. u_c = 18 V, **u_d = 12 V**.
**5. Currents.** R_1 carries 9 A; it divides at c: R_2 gets 9 × 3/(6 + 3) = 3 A, R_3 gets 6 A; at d: **i_4 = 6 × 3/9 = 2 A**, R_x gets 4 A. The current shrinks by 2/3 per section.
**Check:** u_d / R_4 = 12/6 = 2 A ✓; u_d / R_x = 12/3 = 4 A ✓, 2 + 4 = 6 A = the current in R_3 ✓.
